facts.text: Winston‑Salem earned its name in 1851 when the town was renamed after Revolutionary War hero Joseph Winston, replacing its original name Salem.
Old Salem, a Moravian settlement founded in 1766, now serves as a living museum where visitors can see 18th‑century life recreated.
Dubbed the Twin City for its dual heritage and the Camel City for its tobacco past, Winston‑Salem reflects a blend of cultures.
Wake Forest University, founded in 1834, relocated to Winston‑Salem in 1956, bringing a major research institution to the city.
Reynolds Tobacco Company's flagship building, once the tallest south of Baltimore, earned the American Institute of Architects' best building award in its year.
In Old Salem, 70 percent of the original buildings remain, and artisans still practice tinsmithing, blacksmithing, and other crafts for visitors.
